Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The best speed-farming build in the game this season and the only non-Barbarian build Maxroll rates S on both its overall endgame list and its push list. The name is slightly misleading in a way worth fixing up front: the damage is not the Evade. It comes from Pestilent Swarms created by Counterattack running the Lord of Hatred variant Counterattack of the Swarm, and Rushing Claw - with the Evasive Swipe variant, which dashes without needing a target - is used purely as a movement skill. You hold it down and the swarms orbiting you grind through everything you pass. The guide is explicit that Rushing Claw 'doesn't actually count as an Evade, so you can't use Cem', and the whole gearing problem follows from that: every cooldown affix on rings, gloves, helm and amulet exists to shorten Rushing Claw's charge cooldown. Two hard prerequisites: Ring of Writhing Moon, to keep the swarms circling you, and the Prodigy's Tempo paragon board and its legendary node. Because the damage is a damage-over-time, critical strikes cannot crit it, so crit chance is carried only far enough to proc Widow's Web - a genuinely inverted stat priority worth knowing before you gear. The honest counterweight to the S ratings: TierListHQ holds the class at A, 'great at speed, weak at bossing', and this build only partly answers that through Scourge triggering the five-piece set on single targets. And three separate bug situations touch it, which must not be run together. The build deliberately uses one - 'you use Tzic for the 6x damage bug on unstoppable enemies and bosses'. A second constrains it: a Spirit tag inheritance bug means charm +Ranks do not work through Lord of Hatred skill variants, which is why the Berú of Kwatli's Grace set is unusable in most variants; the developers have acknowledged it and a fix missed the Season 14 launch. A third makes Harmony of Ebewaka occasionally drop Ravager below its four-rank minimum. Separately, the Poison Stinger bug in Maxroll's week-1 article belongs to a different Spiritborn build and is not this one's.

Rotation
  1. Activate the secondary cooldowns - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer - then cast both Counterattack charges to raise the swarms, then cast Rushing Claw at packs back and forth.
  2. Keep refreshing cooldowns the moment they are up; movement between packs is manual, so you run.
Variants

Leveling — The guide's own order: activate all the secondary cooldowns - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer - then cast both charges of Counterattack to spin up the swarms, then spam Rushing Claw. Keep refreshing cooldowns as soon as they are up. Expect friction early: 'sometimes Rushing Claw will still be on cooldown and then you will need to run & normal evade for movement while waiting'.
Move on when Loyalty's Mantle in the helm slot. Until then cooldown reduction is a scavenger hunt across rings, gloves, helm and amulet; once it is a crafted Mythic the guide says you no longer need cooldown affixes or tempers at all.

Early Endgame — Unchanged: secondary cooldowns first (Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge, The Devourer), both Counterattack charges to raise the swarms, then hold Rushing Claw through packs and keep refreshing. With Loyalty's Mantle mythic the cooldown gaps close and the movement becomes continuous, which is the whole reason this variant exists.
Move on when 30+ ranks in Ravager. That is the guide's stated requirement for Rushing Claw's Evolving Claws variant, which refills charges permanently from Ferocity - and it is what the next stage is built on.

Late Endgame — The guide rewrites the middle step for this variant: activate the secondary cooldowns, cast both Counterattack charges, then evade or run toward enemy packs and cast Rushing Claw at them back and forth. The difference from earlier stages is that Rushing Claw is now aimed at enemies rather than used as free movement - and it will not refill charges at all if Ravager is below 30 ranks.
Move on when Mythic-tier gear plus a Mythic Talisman seal. At that point the choice is Push for Pit and Tower depth or the Speedfarm branch for sub-two-minute Torment 12 clears - a fork, not a further step.

Pushing — Same opener - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer, then both Counterattack charges - then Rushing Claw into packs. Because Evolving Claws needs targets, movement between packs is manual: you run. The guide is candid that this is precisely why its own cons box calls the push variant 'clunky', and that plus getting stuck on walls is the honest experience of playing it at depth.

Stat requirements
  • It is not recommended to be below 38k Life, if you are pushing for the highest content.
Lootfilter

Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter (in-guide import code) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The guide ships its own filter by name - 'Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter' - as an import code in its Loot Filter section, with sub-toggles including 'HIDE Glaive & QStaff', which matters because this build wants a Polearm specifically. That is the exact match. A name-matching community mirror exists at https://diablo4lootfilter.com/filters/evade-counterswarm-spiritborn-loot-filter-code, but it is a third-party copy that may lag version 2.3 and was confirmed only through search metadata, not by loading the page - prefer the in-guide code.

Uniques
  • ring 1 Target-farm Lord Zir. This is a hard prerequisite, not an upgrade - it is what keeps the swarms circling you rather than left behind. The guide rates it 'your lowest priority in upgrading to a mythic unique', so take the plain Unique and spend your Mythic on the helm instead. Where →
  • helm Target-farm Bartuc. The guide's designated crafted Mythic: 'once you have this as a crafted mythic, you no longer need Cooldown affixes or Tempers', which is the single biggest gearing simplification in the build. Note the string attached - it locks you to Jaguar primary and Jaguar secondary Spirit Halls because of the Spirit tag inheritance bug. Where →
  • helm Target-farm Bartuc. Replaces Loyalty's Mantle at the late endgame and for pushing, which also flips the Spirit Halls to Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary. Carries a known bug: granted skill ranks based on the secondary Spirit Hall occasionally cause Ravager to lose its four-rank minimum when you are at 30 ranks. Where →
  • amulet Target-farm Duriel. Taken for extra AoE damage, and it is the only reason this build carries any critical strike chance at all. It does not combine with Shattered Vow - the guide says plainly 'they don't work together'. Where →

How to run them

Identical across all eight of the guide's variants, and quoted almost verbatim: hire Subo 'for his map hacks and increased damage from Scorched Earth & Incendiary Bolt', reinforce with Raheir's Bastion 'for additional DR & Unstoppable'. The map visibility is not a luxury on a build whose entire point is crossing a map as fast as possible, and Bastion is doing the survivability work that a build with no defensive skill on the bar cannot do for itself.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The best speed-farming build in the game this season and the only non-Barbarian build Maxroll rates S on both its overall endgame list and its push list. The name is slightly misleading in a way worth fixing up front: the damage is not the Evade. It comes from Pestilent Swarms created by Counterattack running the Lord of Hatred variant Counterattack of the Swarm, and Rushing Claw - with the Evasive Swipe variant, which dashes without needing a target - is used purely as a movement skill. You hold it down and the swarms orbiting you grind through everything you pass. The guide is explicit that Rushing Claw 'doesn't actually count as an Evade, so you can't use Cem', and the whole gearing problem follows from that: every cooldown affix on rings, gloves, helm and amulet exists to shorten Rushing Claw's charge cooldown. Two hard prerequisites: Ring of Writhing Moon, to keep the swarms circling you, and the Prodigy's Tempo paragon board and its legendary node. Because the damage is a damage-over-time, critical strikes cannot crit it, so crit chance is carried only far enough to proc Widow's Web - a genuinely inverted stat priority worth knowing before you gear. The honest counterweight to the S ratings: TierListHQ holds the class at A, 'great at speed, weak at bossing', and this build only partly answers that through Scourge triggering the five-piece set on single targets. And three separate bug situations touch it, which must not be run together. The build deliberately uses one - 'you use Tzic for the 6x damage bug on unstoppable enemies and bosses'. A second constrains it: a Spirit tag inheritance bug means charm +Ranks do not work through Lord of Hatred skill variants, which is why the Berú of Kwatli's Grace set is unusable in most variants; the developers have acknowledged it and a fix missed the Season 14 launch. A third makes Harmony of Ebewaka occasionally drop Ravager below its four-rank minimum. Separately, the Poison Stinger bug in Maxroll's week-1 article belongs to a different Spiritborn build and is not this one's.

Rotation
  1. Activate the secondary cooldowns - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer - then cast both Counterattack charges to raise the swarms, then cast Rushing Claw at packs back and forth.
  2. Keep refreshing cooldowns the moment they are up; movement between packs is manual, so you run.
Variants

Leveling — The guide's own order: activate all the secondary cooldowns - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer - then cast both charges of Counterattack to spin up the swarms, then spam Rushing Claw. Keep refreshing cooldowns as soon as they are up. Expect friction early: 'sometimes Rushing Claw will still be on cooldown and then you will need to run & normal evade for movement while waiting'.
Move on when Loyalty's Mantle in the helm slot. Until then cooldown reduction is a scavenger hunt across rings, gloves, helm and amulet; once it is a crafted Mythic the guide says you no longer need cooldown affixes or tempers at all.

Early Endgame — Unchanged: secondary cooldowns first (Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge, The Devourer), both Counterattack charges to raise the swarms, then hold Rushing Claw through packs and keep refreshing. With Loyalty's Mantle mythic the cooldown gaps close and the movement becomes continuous, which is the whole reason this variant exists.
Move on when 30+ ranks in Ravager. That is the guide's stated requirement for Rushing Claw's Evolving Claws variant, which refills charges permanently from Ferocity - and it is what the next stage is built on.

Late Endgame — The guide rewrites the middle step for this variant: activate the secondary cooldowns, cast both Counterattack charges, then evade or run toward enemy packs and cast Rushing Claw at them back and forth. The difference from earlier stages is that Rushing Claw is now aimed at enemies rather than used as free movement - and it will not refill charges at all if Ravager is below 30 ranks.
Move on when Mythic-tier gear plus a Mythic Talisman seal. At that point the choice is Push for Pit and Tower depth or the Speedfarm branch for sub-two-minute Torment 12 clears - a fork, not a further step.

Pushing — Same opener - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer, then both Counterattack charges - then Rushing Claw into packs. Because Evolving Claws needs targets, movement between packs is manual: you run. The guide is candid that this is precisely why its own cons box calls the push variant 'clunky', and that plus getting stuck on walls is the honest experience of playing it at depth.

Stat requirements
  • It is not recommended to be below 38k Life, if you are pushing for the highest content.
Lootfilter

Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter (in-guide import code) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The guide ships its own filter by name - 'Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter' - as an import code in its Loot Filter section, with sub-toggles including 'HIDE Glaive & QStaff', which matters because this build wants a Polearm specifically. That is the exact match. A name-matching community mirror exists at https://diablo4lootfilter.com/filters/evade-counterswarm-spiritborn-loot-filter-code, but it is a third-party copy that may lag version 2.3 and was confirmed only through search metadata, not by loading the page - prefer the in-guide code.

Uniques
  • ring 1 Target-farm Lord Zir. This is a hard prerequisite, not an upgrade - it is what keeps the swarms circling you rather than left behind. The guide rates it 'your lowest priority in upgrading to a mythic unique', so take the plain Unique and spend your Mythic on the helm instead. Where →
  • helm Target-farm Bartuc. The guide's designated crafted Mythic: 'once you have this as a crafted mythic, you no longer need Cooldown affixes or Tempers', which is the single biggest gearing simplification in the build. Note the string attached - it locks you to Jaguar primary and Jaguar secondary Spirit Halls because of the Spirit tag inheritance bug. Where →
  • helm Target-farm Bartuc. Replaces Loyalty's Mantle at the late endgame and for pushing, which also flips the Spirit Halls to Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary. Carries a known bug: granted skill ranks based on the secondary Spirit Hall occasionally cause Ravager to lose its four-rank minimum when you are at 30 ranks. Where →
  • amulet Target-farm Duriel. Taken for extra AoE damage, and it is the only reason this build carries any critical strike chance at all. It does not combine with Shattered Vow - the guide says plainly 'they don't work together'. Where →

Thrillseeker

PassiveSubo

Your active Cooldowns are reduced by 0.5 seconds when an Explosive Charge explodes.

Explosive Charges now detonate after only 1.5 seconds.

Bargaining Chips

PassiveSubo

Targets stuck with Explosive Charges take 5%[x] increased damage per Explosive Charge stuck.

Incendiary Bolt

PassiveSubo

If Subo's Snipe hits the target he originally aimed at, a Molotov explodes on them.

Ambusher

PassiveSubo

You gain 20%[x] Lucky Hit Chance against enemies damaged by Subo's Salvo within the last 3 seconds.

Share a Drink

PassiveSubo

When one of Subo's Molotovs explodes, it has a 50% chance to drop a Healing Potion for you.

Scorched Earth

PassiveSubo

Subo's initial Molotov explosions cause enemies to take 30%[x] increased Damage Over Time from you for 3 seconds.

Mastermind

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Trap and Trip Mines explosions gain 60% Size.

You and Subo gain 25%[+] Crowd Control Duration.

Loaded Munitions

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Traps and Trip Mines inflict Vulnerable on enemies for 5 seconds.

Opening Fire

PassiveSubo

You deal 25%[x] increased Critical Strike Damage to enemies hit by Subo's Cover Fire for 4 seconds.

Pin Cushion

PassiveSubo

Subo's Cover Fire also Immobilizes enemies for 3 seconds.

Ready At Hand

PassiveSubo

Direct damage to an Elite grants you 20%[+] Movement Speed for 2 seconds.

Piercing Arrows

PassiveSubo

Subo's Heavy Shot now pierces through enemies.

Trip Mines

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 18 seconds

Subo scatters 3 explosive traps that each arm after 1.0 seconds. When an enemy moves within range of one, it explodes for 300% Physical damage and Knocks Down enemies for 1.5 seconds.

Cover Fire

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a countless volley of arrows, then unleashes it over your position for 140% Physical damage that Slows enemies by 50% for 4 seconds.

Explosive Charge

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Subo fires 4 Explosive Charges that stick to enemies. Each explodes after 6.5 seconds or when their target dies, dealing 60% Physical damage.

Snipe

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a massive piercing bolt, then unleashes it forwards for 450% Physical damage that Knocks Back enemies.

Wire Trap

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 10 seconds

Weapon: Bow

Basic Attack: Heavy Shot

Subo places a concussive trap that arms after 0.8 seconds. When an enemy moves within range, it explodes for 80% Physical damage and Stuns enemies for 2.0 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo fires a toughened arrow at an enemy, dealing 80% Physical damage with a 30% chance to Stun for 1.0 seconds.

Molotov

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Crossbow

Basic Attack: Salvo

Subo tosses an incendiary at an enemy, dealing 10% Physical damage and Stunning them for 1.0 seconds before exploding into flames. For the next 5 seconds, enemies within the area repeatedly take 36% Burning damage over 3 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo launches 5 bolts at an enemy, each dealing 30% Physical damage. The final bolt explodes, Slowing enemies by 50% for 2 seconds.
